findings.title: OR authorization SQL is not a single parenthesized predicate
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return `(team predicate) OR (user predicate)` with no outer parentheses (the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). getAuthorizationConditions is now the public fragment callers interpolate after findMany was removed. `WHERE <other> AND ${auth}` parses as `(other AND teamBranch) OR userBranch` because AND binds tighter than OR, so the personal-booking branch ignores every predicate the caller ANDs on the left (date range, status, tenant, extra auth). That returns rows outside the intended scope. Wrap the whole OR (and any other returned fragment) in one parenthesis group before returning it.

findings.title: Prisma.sql toEqual assertions do not match nested Sql objects
findings.body: Team scope (line 295), org scope (line 332), and combined filters (line 429) expect one flat Prisma.sql template, but the service builds those strings by nesting Prisma.sql inside reduce (`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})`). Prisma.Sql equality is structural: nested fragments stay as child Sql values with a different `strings` array, so vitest toEqual fails even when the flattened SQL text and bound parameters are what the test author intended. These cases never execute against the database either, so a red run does not tell you whether ANY(${number[]}) is valid. Compare flattened SQL text plus values, or build the expected Sql with the same nesting, and run the team/org fragments through $queryRaw.
